intro.data: The goal is the very thing you started with. You still need a step — but one that changes nothing. One machine returns the spreadsheet untouched; the other smudges it. Predict which, then build the do-nothing step.
intro.alchemy: The goal is the very thing you started with. You still need a step — but one that changes nothing. One apparatus returns the ore untouched; the other taints it. Predict which, then build the do-nothing step.
intro.spellcraft: The goal is the very thing you started with. You still need a step — but one that changes nothing. One rune returns the spark untouched; the other warps it. Predict which, then build the do-nothing step.
intro.abstract: The goal value equals the input. Use the step whose behavior leaves the value unchanged.

goal.data: Send the spreadsheet through a step and get the very same spreadsheet out.
goal.alchemy: Send the ore through a step and get the very same ore out.
goal.spellcraft: Send the spark through a step and get the very same spark out.
goal.abstract: Get the input value back out unchanged.

afterSuccess.data: The Pass Through gave back exactly what went in — a do-nothing step that still counts as a step. The Smudger was the same type, but it changed the value. Identity is the one that truly leaves things alone.
afterSuccess.alchemy: Preserve gave back exactly what went in — a do-nothing step that still counts. The Tainter was the same type but altered the value. Identity truly leaves things alone.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: Echo gave back exactly what went in — a do-nothing step that still counts. The Warper was the same type but altered the essence. Identity truly leaves things alone.
afterSuccess.abstract: Identity returned the value unchanged; the look-alike altered it. Identity is the do-nothing arrow.

reveal.summary: Every object has an identity morphism id_A : A → A that returns each value unchanged. A step that changes nothing is still a real step.
reveal.moreFormal: id_A is the canonical do-nothing arrow on A. Beware look-alikes: being A → A is not enough — identity must leave every value exactly as it found it.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: const idA = (x) => x;  // not the same as a function that quietly mutates x
